title: Standardize engineering artifacts across agents

summary.answer: Put the rule in Semantic contract and delete every caller-side copy. The failure it must stop: a required decision, risk, or validation step disappears because the generated layout changes.
summary.context: Today skills/agent-artifacts/ and src/agent_artifacts/schemas/ each decide which sections an artifact must carry on their own.
summary.what_changes_it: Scenario regression lacks a required semantic section or fails visual review.

context: skills/agent-artifacts/ and src/agent_artifacts/schemas/ each apply the rule in their own way. The check can go missing from one path without a test turning red.
decision: Semantic contract validates context, returns a typed rejection, and reports every outcome to CLI and MCP adapters. No other component may accept.
drivers: One place to change the rule

alternatives.name: Keep checks in each caller
alternatives.summary: Every entry point enforces the rule locally.
alternatives.rejected_because: Preserves the distributed responsibility that caused the failure.

alternatives.name: Centralize in Semantic contract
alternatives.summary: One component owns the contract, rejections, and output.

alternatives.name: Hide it in middleware
alternatives.summary: A generic layer infers context before the domain call.
alternatives.rejected_because: The decision needs explicit context, not transport inference.

consequences.description: One place to verify the behavior: Semantic contract.
CLI and MCP adapters gets one auditable output.
Every caller adopts the contract. No convenience bypass.

reversibility.notes: Callers can return while compatibility code remains. Generated evidence must be rebuilt.
reversibility.reversal_trigger: Two consecutive releases fail on: Scenario regression lacks a required semantic section or fails visual review

validation: Alert fires when scenario regression lacks a required semantic section or fails visual review
A new caller needs no duplicate rules
subtitle: One boundary owns the rule. Callers keep a rollback path until parity holds.
